summary: Discovery focused on security posture and deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Verdant Bio's primary concerns: SOC 2 and ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and enterprise SSO, fine-grained RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS integration, and data residency. Redwood AE/SE explained hosted controls, Dedicated isolation guarantees, and Private/VPC options. Agreed next steps: send SOC2/pen test, schedule technical deep dive, share KMS and networking docs, and provide pricing for Dedicated sizing.
topics: Encryption at rest and KMS/HSM options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we're excited to learn more about Verdant and your security needs. Quick intros?
[00:10] Dr. Elaine Park: Hi this is Elaine, CTO at Verdant Bio. We run sensitive clinical research workloads so security is top priority.
[00:18] Marco Ruiz: Marco here, head of infra, we manage our cloud, VPCs, and EKS clusters.
[00:25] Priya Sharma: Priya, security engineer, I'll be the lead on compliance questions.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Great, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Rafael is our solutions engineer. Rafael?
[00:35] Rafael Ortiz: Hey all - thanks. We'll walk through high level security posture and then dig into specifics - SOC2, SSO, RBAC, KMS, audit logs, retention.
[01:02] Maya Chen: To set expectations, this is very much discovery: are you leaning Hosted/Dedicated/Private? what's required for you to say yes?
[01:18] Dr. Elaine Park: Right now evaluating options. Primary must-haves: SOC2 Type II, enterprise SSO (we use Okta), ability to integrate our KMS or have BYOK, RBAC at role-level, audit logs stored for at least 1 year, and data residency in US-east.
[01:40] Priya Sharma: Also need proof of pen tests and any vulnerability disclosure program.
[01:45] Rafael Ortiz: Totally - we have public SOC2 report and pen test summary we can share. For Hosted, we support SSO via SAML 2.0 and OIDC - Okta is a first-class integration.
[02:02] Marco Ruiz: For Dedicated or Private, we need VPC peering or private networking, and the ability to manage KMS keys - ideally an external HSM or our AWS KMS.
[02:18] Rafael Ortiz: For Dedicated, we provide dedicated GPU pools and network isolation; you can bring your KMS via cross-account roles for AWS KMS. Private (VPC) option gives full control of networking and data plane in your VPC.
[02:40] Dr. Elaine Park: How does RBAC work across teams? we need least privilege for ML engineers vs analysts.
[02:50] Maya Chen: We support RBAC with built-in roles and custom roles. SE: Rafael, can you explain token-level access and auditability?
[02:58] Rafael Ortiz: Sure - at the console and API level we have role-based permissions, you can map SAML attributes to roles. Audit logs capture API calls, model usage, and token metadata. Logs can stream to your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch/GCS - retention configurable, but Hosted default is 90 days; Dedicated and Private allow longer retention and custom retention policies.
[03:30] Priya Sharma: Default 90 days is low for us - we require 12 months. Is that possible on Hosted?
[03:38] Rafael Ortiz: Hosted has add-on log retention packages; we can extend to 12 months for enterprise customers, or you can route logs to your own CloudWatch/Splunk which you control. With Dedicated/Private you can keep logs indefinitely as you manage storage.
[03:55] Marco Ruiz: What's the encryption story - at rest and in transit?
[04:00] Rafael Ortiz: All traffic is TLS in transit. At rest, data is encrypted with AES-256. For Hosted, keys are managed by Redwood by default, but we offer BYOK with AWS KMS or customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. We also support HSM-backed keys for higher assurance.
[04:22] Dr. Elaine Park: And do you have FIPS or HSM certifications?
[04:27] Rafael Ortiz: We can integrate with FIPS-compliant HSMs and AWS KMS in FIPS mode; Redwood's environment itself doesn't carry a FIPS certificate but the underlying managed KMS/HSM can provide that. We'll send the KMS integration guide.
[04:45] Priya Sharma: Audit logs - can we get immutable logs and tamper evidence?
[04:50] Rafael Ortiz: Yes - if you route to your own SIEM or S3 with Object Lock, you get immutability. Our Dedicated offering also has append-only audit storage options and signed event logs.
[05:10] Maya Chen: Any compliance certifications beyond SOC2?
[05:13] Rafael Ortiz: We maintain SOC2 Type II and are working toward ISO 27001; some customers have asked for ISO evidence and we've got a roadmap and partial artifacts we can share.
[05:25] Dr. Elaine Park: Good. What about data residency - specifically we need compute and data to stay in us-east-1 for now.
[05:33] Rafael Ortiz: Hosted supports regional deployments; we can pin your tenant to us-east-1. Dedicated gives you full region-level isolation. Private on-prem obviously stays on-prem.
[05:46] Marco Ruiz: Network connectivity - do you support private link/VPC endpoints?
[05:50] Rafael Ortiz: Yes for Hosted we have PrivateLink and VPC endpoints patterns; Dedicated/Private are colocated in your VPC or connected via private peering.
[06:05] Priya Sharma: Let's talk about data retention & model caching - do you keep prompts or KV cache?
[06:12] Rafael Ortiz: Good question - Redwood does ephemeral KV caching for performance but persistent logs and stored prompts are subject to retention policy. Hosted ephemeral caches are not stored long-term; any persisted request/response logs are part of your retention settings and can be disabled or routed to your storage. We'll clarify in writing.
[06:35] Dr. Elaine Park: We need a legal/Data Processing Agreement clause on retention and deletion - how quickly can data be deleted on request?
[06:42] Maya Chen: We have deletion APIs and SLA'd deletion windows for Dedicated/Private; Hosted deletion is supported but may have a longer processing window - we'll include exact SLAs and language in the DPIA and DPA.
[06:58] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[07:05] Rafael Ortiz: Also to note - for high-sensitivity workloads, customers often choose Dedicated or Private to ensure no co-tenancy and full control of keys and logs. Hosted can meet many enterprise needs if you require fast time-to-value and the add-on security packages.
[07:25] Marco Ruiz: What about pen testing - do you allow a third party test against Dedicated environment?
[07:32] Rafael Ortiz: Typically yes; for Dedicated we can arrange a controlled pen test and share scope; Hosted pen tests are done by Redwood and we can share summaries and remediation reports.
[07:45] Priya Sharma: Does Redwood provide SSO provisioning (SCIM) and SAML attribute mapping?
[07:52] Rafael Ortiz: Yes - SCIM provisioning and SAML attribute mappings for role sync are supported. Okta, Azure AD, G Suite SSO all supported.
[08:05] Maya Chen: Timelines - if you decide on Dedicated, what's the lead time?
[08:10] Rafael Ortiz: Depends on size. Small Dedicated pools can be provisioned in 2-4 weeks; larger enterprise reserved capacity on order of 6-10 weeks depending on GPU types and capacity lead times. We can provide a sizing worksheet.
[08:28] Dr. Elaine Park: Pricing transparency - want clear per-token or per-inference cost and what changes when using Dedicated/Private.
[08:36] Maya Chen: We'll share a price sheet showing hosted per-token, and Dedicated reserved seat pricing. Also call out incremental costs for longer retention, KMS BYOK, and audit log forwarding.
[08:50] Marco Ruiz: How do you handle backups and disaster recovery?
[08:55] Rafael Ortiz: For Dedicated and Private you can adopt your own backup policies. Hosted backups are part of our managed flow with versioned storage; snapshots and model artifacts are stored encrypted. RTO/RPO specifics vary by tier - we'll include SLAs.
[09:12] Priya Sharma: Are there any known tradeoffs around latency vs encryption or RBAC?
[09:18] Rafael Ortiz: Encryption adds negligible latency for TLS/AES. BYOK can add small overhead if keys are remote - but typically microseconds. RBAC checks are cached at session-level to avoid per-request latency. We'll surface performance profiles.
[09:40] Dr. Elaine Park: Can we get a technical deep dive focusing on key management and network topology?
[09:45] Maya Chen: Yes - Rafael can run that. Recommended attendees: Verdant infra, security, and our lead SE.
[09:55] Rafael Ortiz: We'll also propose a POC: start with Hosted trial, then if needed spin Dedicated pilot for isolated workloads and run a short benchmark.
[10:08] Marco Ruiz: For the POC, we want to validate throughput and cost for our 2k tokens/req workloads and ensure KV caching behaves as expected.
[10:16] Rafael Ortiz: We'll capture sample load and simulate with our bench harness - share a template for the perf test.
[10:24] Priya Sharma: Any regulatory concerns for clinical data?
[10:28] Rafael Ortiz: Redwood can support HIPAA-covered use when configured appropriately (BAA in place); we'll share checklist for PHI handling.
[10:36] Dr. Elaine Park: Great. On the SOC2 and ISO topic - you mentioned ISO in progress; how mature is that program?
[10:44] Rafael Ortiz: We're mid-way; we have formalized policies and some audits complete. We can share roadmap and expected dates.
[10:52] Maya Chen: Let's confirm deliverables and next steps.
[10:56] Dr. Elaine Park: Sounds good.
[11:00] Maya Chen: Action items: I'll send SOC2 and pen test artifacts; Rafael will schedule tech deep dive and send RBAC/KMS docs; Marco will share network diagram. We'll aim to have those by the dates discussed.
[11:14] Priya Sharma: One last Q - do you support customer-managed logging endpoints with signed events?
[11:20] Rafael Ortiz: Yes - signed events and streaming to your account is supported. We'll include sample CloudWatch and Splunk configs.
[11:30] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links.
[11:35] Dr. Elaine Park: Thanks, talk soon.
[11:40] (meeting ends)
